item.title: State lawmakers continued to discuss NYSERDA memo
item.description: New Yorkers from around the state still had questions on Tuesday following last week's New York State Energy Research and Development Authority's (NYSERDA) memo release. The circulated memo made plainly the potential energy utility cost increases that New Yorkers could face if the 2019 Climate Leadership & Community Protection Act (CLCPA) continued as is.

item.title: New York bills would increase low-income lending
item.description: New York state officials have proposed two laws to help minority-owned and local banks lend more money in low-income neighborhoods, by updating how the state deposits public money into local banks and increasing the maximum deposit a single bank can receive.

item.title: LoMedico issues apology after fire department comments
item.description: A member of the Utica Common Council has issued an apology after insensitive comments they made at last week's meeting.

item.title: New York Comptroller urges Big Tech to pay for upgrades
item.description: New York State Comptroller Thomas DiNapoli has sent letters to Big Tech executives, urging them to pay for their own local power and infrastructure upgrades rather than passing costs down to consumers, and to enact internal policies that responsibly guide data center construction and leasing to prevent damaging local resources or public services.

item.title: NYSERDA memo talks continue
item.description: With the state budget due in just under a month, discussions about the NYSERDA memo that surfaced last week continued on Wednesday. Last week, a memo circulated that projected grim utility/energy costs New Yorkers could pay with the current state of New York's Climate Leadership and Community Protection Act.
